# PIR-2026-004: A 42-minute utility outage: generators carried the site with no IT impact

**Status:** Action items closed · **Blameless review:** findings describe systems and procedures, not individuals. Interactive version: [Post-Incident Review page](https://jasonmossotti.github.io/dco-vendor-scorecard/pir/).

*OSR 1 (Negligible): Recorded and reported, little or no obvious impact on business services, no service disruptions. No IT service was disrupted: the UPS systems carried the load through the transfer and the generators carried the site until the utility came back. Reviewed because losing the utility is the event the site's whole power design exists for.*

## In plain language

**What happened?** On the afternoon of September 24 the utility feeding the site failed. Both of the site's incoming medium-voltage breakers tripped, the standby generators took the site over within seconds, and the utility came back 42 minutes later. No rack lost power at any point.

**Who was affected?** Nobody. No rack, no GPU, and no customer-facing service was affected, and nobody was hurt. The site ran on generators for 42 minutes.

**Why did it happen?** The cause was outside the site: the utility lost voltage on its own network. Under the Interface Agreement a utility outage is attributed to the utility, and the Landlord is measured on carrying the load, which it did.

**What are we doing about it?** Nothing about the response needs to change. The review confirmed the two things worth confirming: that all seven generators started and carried the site, and that the return to the utility was made without a second interruption. The Landlord's own records of the transfer agreed with the site data.

## Summary (technical)

At 2026-09-24T21:14:20Z both the MV-A and MV-B main breakers tripped on utility undervoltage. The generator paralleling bus was live with 7 of 7 generators at 21:14:30Z, 10 seconds later, and the generator tie breakers closed to MV-A and MV-B at 21:14:32Z; the UPS systems carried the IT load across the gap. WO-41009 was opened at 21:15:29Z and acknowledged in 2 minutes (P1 target 5); an engineer was at the MV switchgear in 8 minutes (P1 target 15). The utility returned at 21:56:06Z and both mains closed in a closed-transition retransfer, with the generator tie breakers opening 5 seconds later, so the site returned to the utility without a second interruption. Measured restoration is 42 min from the trip, which matches the work order; the Landlord recorded 10.5 MW carried on generators. Under FA-6 the event is Utility-attributed, with no capacity lost and no IT Partner clock. No finding was raised.

- **Trigger:** Loss of voltage on the 138 kV utility service feeding the site.
- **Detection:** Immediate and automatic: both MV main breakers tripped on undervoltage and the generators started without a human decision; the work order was opened 69 seconds later.
- **Resolution:** The generators carried the site for 42 minutes; when the utility returned, both mains closed in a closed-transition retransfer and the generator ties opened 5 seconds later.

## Contract and compliance consequences


## EHS screening

- **Injuries:** 0
- **Screening:** Automatic transfer with no manual switching on energised equipment; the engineer attended to observe. No injury, no arc flash, nothing to refer under EHS-R2.
- **Referral:** None. Screened and closed by the Customer Site Lead.

## Contributing factors

| ID | Type | Factor |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | External | The utility lost voltage on its own network. The site has no control over this and the design assumes it: this is what the generators and the UPS systems are for. |
| F2 | Equipment | All seven generators started and paralleled within 10 seconds, and the UPS systems carried the IT load across the gap. The monthly generator tests are what makes that reliable, which is why finding L-003 on a test record matters even when no outage follows it. |

## What went well

- The transfer was automatic and complete in 12 seconds: bus live at 10 seconds, ties closed at 12.
- All 7 of 7 generators ran, and the Landlord recorded 10.5 MW carried.
- The return to the utility was a closed transition, so there was no second interruption when the utility came back.
- The work order's own times and the site's electrical data agreed on the trip and the restoration to the second.

## What went poorly

- Nothing in the response. The review notes only that the site's confidence in this transfer rests on the monthly generator tests, and that one test record in the same month did not reconcile (finding L-003, GEN-4).

## Where we got lucky

- Nothing turned on luck: the event ran the way the design intends. The utility outage was also short enough that fuel was never a question.
